content:
One of the most frustrating elements of the iPhone user interface is that we have to play a guessing game in order to change an application's settings.

Sometimes we open the application and go to its built-in settings menu. But other times, we have to exit the application and open the completely separate Apple "Settings" app, which is not exactly a good experience (although there is a free shortcut that can help)...

The Problem with Settings

We've all experienced this situation. We want to change an application's settings, so we go to the "hamburger menu," select "Settings," and look for what we want. When we can't find it, we then realise we need to exit the app, open Apple's own "Settings" app, search for the application, change the setting there, and finally reopen the app we originally wanted to use.

This process is already cumbersome in itself, and the worst part is that we still have to guess where to look, making the whole thing even more troublesome.

Take Apple's own "Camera" app as an example. Recent iPhones offer what Apple calls Fusion Camera for the 1x lens. Its default focal length is 24mm, but we can actually change the default to 28mm or 35mm. This is done by having the app automatically crop the image. In addition, we can also choose whether or not to tap the "1x" button to cycle through different focal lengths.

But unless it's tucked away in a place I haven't discovered, we simply cannot make this setting within the "Camera" app. Instead, we have to open the "Settings" app, scroll down to "Camera,"* then scroll down to the "Photo Capture" section, tap "Fusion Camera"—only after completing these steps can we select the option we want.

*Not to mention that we still have to guess whether an Apple app will have its own section in "Settings" or be placed under the "Apps" section...

A Shortcut Offers a Partial Solution

We can't avoid the guessing part, but at least there's a handy third-party shortcut created by Quinn Nelson of Snazzy Labs that can ease the pain a little.

Thanks to John Gruber for pointing this out to me. Thank you. If you want to install it yourself:

  • Download and install it here
  • Open Control Centre
  • Tap the + icon in the top left corner
  • Tap "Add a Control" at the bottom
  • Search for "Shortcut"
  • Tap "Run Shortcut"
  • Select the "App Settings" shortcut

After installation is complete, if you're using an app and find you need to look for settings in the separate "Settings" app, you simply need to swipe down from the top right corner to open Control Centre, then tap the App Settings button.

But Apple Should Officially Solve This Problem

However, I'd much rather see a proper solution rather than a handy third-party workaround.

My suggestion is that every application's settings menu should have a "More" option at the bottom—which would then automatically open the "Settings" app and jump to the correct page. This way, if we can't find something in the app's own settings menu, it would only take one extra tap.

To be clear, Apple already provides an API to do this, but relatively few developers use it. I hope Apple can make this a mandatory requirement.

Is there anything you'd like to see? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
